subject: how to set the number of mappers in the mapreduce function

messages.author: 39e37739a45d1c94
messages.subject: how to set the number of mappers in the mapreduce function
parts:
Hi,

I am pretty new to the RHadoop package. Previously, I use snow and mulitcore a lot, and there is a parameter to set the number of process for the parallelization.

However, in the RHadoop packages, I cannot find it. And it seems everytime, it only initialize two mappers.

I am wondering is there any ways to set the number of mappers? Or how to maximum the parallelization explicitly.

Ben

messages.author: 6ac7e7dfbe4f6c38
messages.subject: Re: [RHadoop:#924] how to set the number of mappers in the mapreduce function
parts:
You can try using a deprecated feature, backend.parameters, but hadoop won't necessarily follow it. You can also set it at the hadoop configuration level, which is the recommended way in most cases. Strangely enough some hadoop distributions come with a default of 2, but the default should be related to the size of your cluster. See your hadoop distribution docs for details. As the capacity scheduler becomes more widely adopted I hope there will be a better way of accommodating jobs with different resource requirements.


Antonio
